text:
Situation: As of 2026-10-21, potassium chloride is not on FDA's current shortage list. FDA's history shows an earlier shortage first posted on 2021-11-02 that has since resolved. The drug carries a "To Be Discontinued" status since 2021-11-02. Corvale East holds only 2.7 days of POTASSIUM CHLORIDE 29.8G000ML 50ML BAG (35 on hand) and 6.1 days of Potassium Chloride 750 mg/1 at Corvale Lakeside (13 on hand). Other presentations at Corvale East and Corvale General hold 8.9 to 22 days. Corvale General holds 16.4 days of the 29.8 g/1000 mL, 50 mL bags (215 on hand).

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 1075479 ended 2018-12-21, classified VAI, 1047 days before the 2021-11-02 shortage posting. Inspection 1106244 ended 2019-09-06, classified OAI, classification letter dated 2020-05-25, 788 days before posting. Inspection 1110899 ended 2019-11-21, classified VAI, classification letter dated 2020-02-12, 712 days before posting. Inspection 1121028 ended 2020-02-28, classified VAI, classification letter dated 2020-04-17, 613 days before posting. A Warning Letter was issued 2020-03-25, 587 days before posting.

Our position: No active FDA shortage exists. The "To Be Discontinued" status dates to 2021-11-02. Internal distribution imbalances create risk at Corvale East and Corvale Lakeside for specific presentations. Corvale General holds sufficient surplus to support transfers.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 31 bags of 29.8 g/1000 mL, 50 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 18 tablets of 750 mg from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside — approved by Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
3. Transfer 18 tablets of 750 mg from Corvale General to Corvale Lakeside — approved by Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
4. Transfer 19 units of 14.9 g/100 mL, 250 mL from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — approved by Pharmacy Director (transfer request).
5. Evaluate purchase from ICU Medical Inc. (not on FDA shortage list; plants: Otsuka ICU Medical LLC last inspection VAI 2017-03-10; ICU Medical) — approved by Buyer.

Not recommended: No clinical protocol changes; those remain with treating clinicians and the committee.
